instruction: I tried executing "sdkman version" in terminal and got "sdk: command not found". Could you help me solve this so I can use SDKMAN commands right away?

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

result.command: grep -q 'THIS MUST BE AT THE END OF THE FILE FOR SDKMAN' ~/.bashrc && echo 1 || echo 0

metadata.explanation: Task requires fixing 'sdk: command not found' by adding SDKMAN initialization to ~/.bashrc. Evaluator checks for the characteristic SDKMAN comment line that appears when it's properly initialized. Similar complexity to original conda task.
metadata.verification_notes: Used existing exact_match metric and vm_command_line getter. Checked for SDKMAN's characteristic initialization comment in .bashrc.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete verification: Only checks for SDKMAN comment line in ~/.bashrc, not actual SDKMAN initialization code or functionality
False positive risk: A user could manually add just the comment string without actual SDKMAN code, and evaluator would pass
Missing functionality check: Instruction requires SDKMAN to work 'right away', but evaluator doesn't verify that sdk commands are actually executable
Missing installation verification: Doesn't check if SDKMAN is actually installed on the system
Missing session state: Even if code is in ~/.bashrc, it won't work in current terminal without sourcing - evaluator doesn't verify this
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Change verification command to actually test if sdk command works: 'sdk version' or 'which sdk' or 'command -v sdk'
If checking ~/.bashrc, verify the actual SDKMAN initialization code exists (e.g., grep for 'source.*sdkman-init.sh'), not just the comment
Consider checking both: (1) SDKMAN installation exists AND (2) sdk command is available in PATH
To verify 'right away' requirement, test that sdk command executes successfully in the current context
